b: Friday, November 20, 2026 brought a quieter flow of news and a clear message from China's two biggest online marketplaces: the spending war is cooling. Alibaba cut sales and marketing costs by 38% in its latest quarter while revenue from merchants on Taobao and Tmall fell 5%, and Temu's owner PDD cut marketing by 17% as revenue stalled, even as its own advertising income overtook commissions. In the West, AI assistants started doing a job coupon sites have done for two decades, serving promo codes straight into answers a week before Black Friday. Google told advertisers that ad surcharges in France and Italy will rise in January and Brazil will get a new one, Google Analytics let marketers plan budgets by individual ad platform, and Google's head of Search said thin pages are losing their audience in AI search. Amazon Web Services moved fraud screening and device data inside its private auction network, Databricks lined up nine ad platforms to receive customer-value signals, and Brazil's privacy regulator named eight kinds of platform presumed to fall under its child safety law. Holiday advertising went back to basics: Coca-Cola dropped AI imagery from its seasonal spot and Meta pitched smart glasses to parents. The day's thread was retreat and redeployment, as companies pulled money from one place to put it somewhere they could measure better.

The Landline newsletter can also be heard. Marketing Is Calling reads each edition aloud every day, on Spotify, Apple Podcasts and YouTube. Marketing Rodeo picks the most controversial advertising story of each day, weekends included, and has some fun with it, on Spotify, Apple Podcasts and YouTube.
China's marketplaces stop paying for growth

Alibaba's quarter showed a company spending far less to keep shoppers and earning far more from computing. PPC Land reported that Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall merchant revenue dropped 5% as cloud jumped 53% in the quarter to September 30. Group revenue rose 10% to RMB271.5bn. Customer management revenue, the money merchants pay Alibaba on Taobao and Tmall, much of it for advertising and search placement, fell 5% to RMB75.0bn, about $11.2bn. Alibaba said it grew 1% on a like-for-like basis once a new business development programme, which books some subsidies as a reduction in revenue, is stripped out. PPC Land estimated that accounting effect at RMB4bn to RMB5bn.

The cost line moved further. Sales and marketing expenses fell 38% to RMB41.3bn from RMB66.5bn, dropping from 26.8% of revenue to 15.2%. The money is going into computing instead: AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue rose 53% to RMB61.0bn, adjusted earnings for that unit rose 121% to RMB8.8bn, and capital spending climbed 60% to RMB50.5bn, leaving free cash flow negative at RMB34.5bn. Management set a target of 30% to 45% cloud growth for fiscal 2028, but said it could not yet estimate the effect of a US export rule issued on November 16.

Alibaba's executives described a more careful shopper. "Consumers are becoming more cautious in their spending, and certain categories continue to face intense competition," said Jiang Fan, chief executive of the e-commerce business group, speaking through an interpreter. Eddie Wu, the group chief executive, pointed to a new merchant agent launched in October: "We recently launched QwenWork E-Commerce, and the percentage of paying e-commerce users continues to rise." He also warned about where AI applications are heading: "if all the apps are basically running on the same model, then those apps are very easy to replicate." International e-commerce revenue fell 8% to RMB25.7bn, mainly because of AliExpress and the European Union's customs reform, and Alibaba booked a provision for a EUR550m Digital Services Act fine tied to AliExpress. It disclosed no gross merchandise volume, take rate or advertising breakdown.

Temu's owner told a similar story from a different angle. PPC Land reported that Temu owner PDD cut marketing spend 17% as revenue stalled. Revenue was flat at RMB108.3bn, about $16.2bn, in the quarter to September 30. Inside that total, the balance shifted: online marketing services and other revenue rose 12% to RMB59.8bn, while transaction services, mostly commissions, fell 12% to RMB48.5bn. A year earlier, commissions had been the larger line. PDD has, in effect, become more of an advertising company than a commission business.

Sales and marketing expenses fell 16.6% to RMB25.3bn, and total operating expenses fell 12%, while research and development rose 16.8% to RMB5.1bn. Operating profit climbed 24.5% to RMB31.2bn, lifting the operating margin to 28.8% from 23.1%. Yet net income attributable to shareholders rose only 0.7% to RMB29.5bn, because interest and investment income fell 37.1% and income tax rose 64.8%. The release did not explain the swing between revenue lines, the tax increase or a RMB9.5bn nine-month loss under other items, and it gave no split between Pinduoduo and Temu.

PDD's executives played down the quarter. "Single-quarter metrics should not be extrapolated as a reliable indicator of future trends," said Jun Liu, vice president of finance. Co-chief executive Jiazhen Zhao said of the competitive field that "no platform is pulling back," while Lei Chen, the other co-chief executive, acknowledged the strain on sellers: "SME merchants are indeed facing considerable pressure and challenges." PPC Land set the results beside JD.com's 26% marketing cut and the European Union's duty and Digital Services Act actions against Temu. For Western ad platforms that have counted Chinese marketplaces among their biggest buyers, both reports point the same way: less money spent on acquiring shoppers, more effort spent on logistics, merchants and owned advertising.
AI answers start handing out the codes

The coupon business may be the next to feel the force of AI answers. Search Engine Roundtable reported that Google, ChatGPT and other AI engines now provide coupon codes directly in their answers, so shoppers can copy a code without visiting a coupon site. Glenn Gabe and Metehan Yesilyurt shared screenshots. Gabe said the free version of ChatGPT shows coupon cards with a "copy code" button, while the paid version gave codes without cards. "That's concerning... Then users wouldn't have to click through," Gabe wrote.

Yesilyurt described a ChatGPT answer to a web hosting coupon query that returned a card for each brand, Bluehost, Hostinger, Cloudways, HostPapa and another host, each with a discount, a price, an end date of December 7, a code with a Copy button and a "Get deal" button. One code, BLACKFRIDAYREDDIT, appeared to come from community or affiliate pages. Google's AI Mode listed codes as text with source cards from HostAdvice, Reddit and Hostinger, and Claude listed them as text citing Gizmodo and Cybernews. Yesilyurt summed up what is at stake for coupon publishers, whose model, he wrote, is the click: a visitor arrives for the code, the site sets a cookie and earns the commission. He was unsure whether ChatGPT's cards were a test or a rollout, and advised coupon sites to track which codes appear and to promote exclusive codes, and brands to publish current codes on official promotion pages.

Barry Schwartz noted that Google has shown coupon-style content in ads for about a decade, through promotion extensions, clippable coupons and loyalty codes, and that merchants already supply codes through structured data that can feed Search, Shopping, AI Overviews and agentic checkout in AI Mode. He recalled that coupon sites were hit by Google's site reputation abuse policy and asked whether withholding codes from bots could lead to penalties. With Black Friday on November 27, the timing could hardly be sharper for affiliate publishers.

OpenAI may also be reshaping its front door. Search Engine Roundtable reported that OpenAI is testing a card design on ChatGPT, a "try something new" panel that previews functions such as news cards, comics, event planning, meeting agendas, cooking help, travel itineraries, book recommendations and quizzes. Radu Oncescu spotted it on November 16: "OpenAI seems to be rolling out the new "Nova" interface for ChatGPT users on desktop (web) and non-logged-in," he wrote. OpenAI made no statement. A home screen that suggests tasks rather than waiting for a query would push more users towards the shopping and planning prompts that advertisers care about.

Google's head of Search offered her own view of what survives in AI search. PPC Land reported that shallow pages draw less interest in AI search, Google's Liz Reid says, in an interview on Patrick McGinnis's FOMO Sapiens podcast. Reid said interest is falling in pages that only restate surface facts, while content built on expertise, personal experience, community or in-depth research still draws an audience. "People don't want purely AI, they want AI in the web," she said. Her test for publishers was whether a human would actually want to read a page "or is it just a means to an end?"

Reid named preferred sources and creator follows as Google's tools for connecting publishers and users, said videos rank higher in India than in the US for the same query because of heavier voice and video use, and said AI Overviews were held to the featured-snippet quality bar at launch. She gave no traffic, click or revenue figures and declined to give her team's size. PPC Land set her comments against studies she did not address: a field experiment that found AI Mode users clicked through to outside sites 18.8 percentage points less often, research showing AI Overviews cut outbound organic clicks by 39.8%, and an Ahrefs finding of 58% lower click-through rates for top pages. Preferred sources passed 600,000 unique sources by August 20, 2026.

The search industry may soon get an address of its own. Search Engine Roundtable reported that a .seo top-level domain may be coming soon. XYZ.COM LLC, which operates .xyz, applied for it in ICANN's new round of generic domains, and it was confirmed on the final list after String Confirmation Day in October. Only one application was filed, so no auction is needed. Domaintechnik.at expects "a launch possible no earlier than late 2027 and open registration realistically in 2028." Schwartz reminded readers that Google treats new top-level domains like any generic domain, with no ranking benefit.
Google adjusts the bill and the plan

Google advertisers in four countries will see different surcharges from January. PPC News Feed reported that Google Ads is adjusting surcharges for France, Italy, Turkey and Brazil from January 1, 2027. The Regulatory Operating Costs surcharge in France rises from 2% to 3%, Italy's rises from 2.5% to 3%, Brazil gets a new 2.9% surcharge, and Turkey's falls from 4.5% to 2.25%. "These changes impact advertisers based on where their ads are served, not their business location," the report said, and the increases in France and Italy "reflect the costs for complying with Digital Services Taxes." Advertisers receive notification emails, and 2027 invoices will show the new rates. Thomas Eccel spotted the change, which PPC Times also reported. For a brand spending heavily in France, a one-point rise on top of the media price is a cost increase that no bidding strategy can optimise away.

Planning tools are getting more granular. PPC Land reported that ad platforms get their own line in Google Analytics budget plans. The cross-channel budgeting tool, in beta since January 16, 2026, can now break plans down by individual ad platform rather than only by channel group, so paid social can be split into Meta, TikTok and Pinterest. "Cross-channel budgeting in Google Analytics now supports source platform dimensions," Google Analytics said on LinkedIn. Projection plans track in-flight performance against a budget, conversion or revenue target, while scenario plans build future media plans.

The fine print matters. The help page says the tools are for planning purposes only and will not change budgets or spend in connected ad accounts. A model based on data-driven attribution needs at least a year of campaign data from at least two channels, one of them non-Google, and a model based on Meridian, Google's open-source media mix model, needs two years of cost, conversion and revenue data and is limited to select Analytics 360 customers. Non-Google cost data arrives through campaign data import. One illustrated scenario projected conversions up 17.36% while cost per conversion rose 19.21%, from $21.14 to $25.20. PPC Land noted that the LinkedIn post's claim of "real time" pacing conflicts with the help page's weekly pacing reviews, and that the documentation lists no rollout timeline or recognised platforms.

Demand Gen campaigns are losing a layer of settings. PPC News Feed reported that campaign-level Display targeting is changing for Demand Gen. From the week of December 1, campaign-level Display targeting will be on by default for new Demand Gen campaigns, and Display targeting will be managed only at ad group level through channel controls. "Previously, disabling Display targeting at the campaign level overrode ad group settings," the report noted. Existing campaigns with Display turned off will be updated at ad group level to match, across the Google Ads API, interface and Editor. Advertisers who keep Display off should check that the ad group settings still reflect that choice after the switch.
Plumbing for the auction and the signal

Amazon's cloud business is moving deeper into the mechanics of programmatic buying. PPC Land reported that AWS puts fraud filters and device data inside the ad auction. On November 19, Amazon Web Services opened RTB Fabric Modules to buyers through AWS Marketplace, letting ad tech firms attach third-party data such as fraud screening, device details and placement quality scores to bid requests as they cross AWS's private auction network, with vendor charges on the AWS bill. The launch vendors are Pixalate, WURFL by ScientiaMobile and Picnic, and AWS says a signal deploys in minutes rather than the weeks or months a custom integration takes.

Pixalate's module filters invalid traffic before it reaches the bidder and adds show, channel, genre and rating data to connected TV requests, covering more than 770,000 US streaming shows and 17,900 FAST and linear channels. Amin Bandeali, Pixalate's chief technology officer, claimed the approach can cut "wasted compute by up to 15%." WURFL draws on more than 120,000 device profiles, and Picnic scores inventory across more than 100 signals. "Modules let a partner's signal reach our bid path through configuration instead of a lengthy engineering project," said Keith Petri of Viant, a customer. The details carry caveats: the default quota is two modules per flow, so a standard link can run only two of the three launch modules; vendor modules fail open, letting traffic through if a module breaks; and AWS disclosed no module prices or regions. RTB Fabric launched in October 2025, and Axel Springer reported median bid latency falling from 45 to 80 milliseconds to under 10. Index Exchange, PubMatic and the IAB Tech Lab have rival approaches.

The data warehouse wants a direct line to the ad platforms too. PPC Land reported that Databricks lined up nine ad platforms for its customer-value signals. CustomerLake Conversions, part of the agentic customer data platform Databricks launched in June, lets brands send value-weighted conversion signals based on purchase history, margin and predicted lifetime value. The nine launch partners are Amazon Ads, Google, LinkedIn, Meta, Microsoft Ads, Reddit, Snapchat, The Trade Desk and TikTok. "Marketers still define success; CustomerLake helps translate those priorities into signals advertising platforms can use," Databricks wrote, arguing that "the only lever advertisers fully control is what signals they feed them." No release date or price was given, the examples carried no performance figures or named customers, and consent handling and hashing were not addressed.

Together, the two launches show the infrastructure companies competing for a role the ad platforms have long kept for themselves. AWS wants to own the pipes that bid requests travel through, and Databricks wants to own the data that tells bidding algorithms what a customer is worth. Both pitch speed and control, and both leave the hardest questions, about price, privacy and proof of results, for later.
Holiday ads go back to people

The world's most famous holiday advertiser stepped back from AI. Adweek reported that AI is off the festive dinner menu in Coke's 2026 holiday ad. "Enjoy Joy," a 30-second spot, shows a traditional holiday gathering at a white country farmhouse, where friends, family and strangers share food, games and bottles of Coke. It uses no AI-generated imagery and has no polar bears. Adweek presented it as a return to human-centred storytelling after two years in which Coca-Cola's holiday work used AI-generated trucks and creatures, describing the look as "pure Norman Rockwell's America." The spot also runs in 15- and 6-second cutdowns and in English and Spanish versions.

Meta took the opposite path, putting technology at the centre of the family moment. Adweek reported that Meta's holiday ad pitches its smart glasses as the secret to present parenting. The campaign, "Stay in the Moment," made by Mother LA, shows the glasses "helping parents capture their kids' school holiday plays without looking through a phone screen." It runs across social and out-of-home and features Meta Glasses, Ray-Ban Meta and Ray-Ban Meta Audio. Last year Meta returned to holiday advertising with a Messenger campaign; this year it is selling a product Adweek called controversial, given the privacy questions around cameras worn on the face.

Brands are also building their own entertainment. Adweek reported how Taco Bell turned a golf tournament into its latest entertainment play. The first Live Mas Open, held in Laguna Beach, California, earlier in November and hosted by Kevin Hart, had qualifying entrants compete for the chance to bring a discontinued menu item back to restaurants nationwide, alongside celebrities, athletes and creators on a Taco Bell-themed course. The event streams on Peacock from November 20, with a Golf Channel debut later in the month. It extends Live Mas Live, the brand's annual showcase of new menu items, which began three years ago.

The merged Hollywood studio has a new marketing map. Adweek reported that Skydance's Rebecca Mall announced a new marketing leadership team, the latest unit to reorganise since Skydance acquired Warner Bros. Discovery in October. In a staff memo, Mall, the chief marketing officer, described a group combining creativity, data and technology. "We have an incredible opportunity to build a more unified, innovative and effective marketing organization," she wrote, promising a structure that "breaks down silos." Annah Zafrani leads cross-company marketing and corporate brand, Angie Sharma leads franchise and kids and family, Jamal Salmon leads marketing data and analytics, Michelle Hagen leads brand partnerships, and Seth Goren, from Warner Bros. Discovery, leads media strategy, buying and agency management. Meg Maro, global head of franchise, is leaving.

A TV ad tech joint venture is shrinking its role. AdExchanger reported that Ampersand is offloading its independent agency business to Comcast and Spectrum following mass layoffs. Ampersand, formed in 2019 by Comcast, Charter and Cox and now owned by Charter, will hand independent agencies to Comcast Advertising and Charter's Spectrum Reach from January 1, 2027, keeping its focus on the largest agency groups and political advertising. A client memo said the new model "will give independent agencies more direct access" to Comcast and Spectrum Reach inventory, data and measurement. A source described several significant unannounced layoffs, and Glassdoor reviews mention "mass layoffs over the past two years." Ampersand denied it is shutting down and confirmed affected roles without detail. AdImpact puts 2026 midterm political spending at $12.06bn, the first midterm cycle to outspend a presidential one, though that revenue is highly cyclical.
Brazil writes the rules for children online

Brazil's privacy regulator set out who must comply with its child safety law. PPC Land reported that Brazil's ANPD named eight platform types presumed to face its child safety law, in an English edition of its 69-page guidance on the Digital Statute for Children and Adolescents, Law No. 15,211, which has applied since March 17, 2026. The eight categories presumed likely to be accessed by children are social media, app stores, operating systems, services with editorial control, video games, adult content, generative AI systems and e-commerce selling goods banned to minors. "Likely access is presumed unless proven otherwise," the guidance says, and that presumption "may only be rebutted with proper justification."

The law applies wherever a provider is based, including free services funded by advertising. Age assurance does not take a provider out of scope, and self-assessments do not bind the regulator. Providers with more than 1,000,000 registered child and adolescent users in Brazil must file transparency reports twice a year, and Article 35 allows fines of up to R$50m per infraction. The guidance follows an August order against Discord and a recommendation of R$153.7m in fines against ByteDance. Thresholds for "number of users" and "size of the provider" remain undefined, which leaves ad-funded apps with large young audiences guessing how far their duties extend. The document says the English translation was generated with AI, and the Portuguese original prevails.

Month is a time dimension in Amazon Ads unified reporting that sums impressions, clicks, spend and sales across each calendar month instead of day by day. Unified reporting launched in beta on November 11, 2025 with six years of monthly data.

Date range is a time field in Amazon Ads unified reporting that shows the first and last day of the period a row's figures cover. Amazon DSP added a time breakdown with daily, weekly, monthly and day-of-week views on October 6, 2022.

Benchmark browse category ID holds the browse node code for the product category that defines a campaign's Amazon benchmark peer group. Benchmarks reached general availability in 18 markets on May 18, 2026.

Stalking horse bid is an initial, binding offer for a distressed company or some of its assets, agreed before an auction so later bidders have a price to beat. Near Intelligence filed in Delaware on December 8, 2023 with a lender stalking horse credit bid of at least $50m.

Debtor-in-possession describes a business in US Chapter 11 that still runs its own operations under court supervision instead of handing control to a trustee. The Bankruptcy Reform Act that created the modern Code was signed on November 6, 1978.

Consumer privacy ombudsman is a disinterested person appointed in a US bankruptcy case to advise the judge when a debtor wants to sell customers' personal data. The role was added to the Bankruptcy Code by a law signed on April 20, 2005.
